## License

Every recording is dedicated to the public domain under **CC0 1.0** (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/), as shown on its Freesound page on 2026-10-02. CC0 allows copying, modifying and distributing, including commercially, without permission or credit. The pack is `CC0-1.0`; the credit in `pack.json` is a courtesy. CC0 does not grant trademark rights, so the pack's name avoids brand names and the hardware is named only to describe the recordings. The StavSounds pack page (https://freesound.org/people/StavSounds/packs/42151/) also lists each of the 12 taps as "Creative Commons 0" (10 of them are used, see "Not used"), and clatterbox's `CREDITS.md` (below) says each file's page was checked one by one.

## Each take is a whole tap

Every recording holds one tap: the key-down, then the key-up after the finger's dwell, 80–180 ms later, with a quiet gap between them (clatterbox ships the takes as they are, as key-down sounds). Played whole on key-down, each would also sound a key-up at a fixed delay, whenever the key is actually released. So the build splits each take in two (`packlib.split_tap`): the key-up is the loudest moment at least 60 ms after the key-down starts, its attack starts where the level (1 ms frames, walking back from that peak) first drops 20 dB below it, and the split is the middle of the quietest 5 ms between 30 ms after the key-down and 1 ms before that attack. The build stops unless that gap is at least 24 dB (RMS) below the key-up's peak. The key-down becomes the press sound and the same take's key-up its release sound: every release is a recorded key-up, none is made up. The key-up sound starts 5 ms before its attack (or at the split, if that is later); what lies between the split and there (up to 52 ms, a soft noise in some takes) is left out, so that no key-up starts that far ahead of its click. Both strokes are cut against the whole take's noise floor.

## Levelling

The StavSounds takes were recorded at very different strengths: as recorded, the key-downs of all 12 takes span 19.8 dB of loudness, and those of the 10 used takes 14.2 dB. With one gain for all of them, the typical keystroke played far below the few loudest ones (and below the other packs). Loudness here is what `synth-packs loudness` measures per sample: the K-weighted (ITU-R BS.1770) energy of the first 100 ms (`packlib.k_loudness`, on the stroke as cut at unity gain). Each take gets one levelling gain (`level_gain_db`), the smallest that puts its key-down within 3 dB of the median take's key-down (-30.9 LK as recorded) and its key-up no louder than the top of that band. A take already inside the band keeps its recorded level, so the natural variation within ±3 dB stays, and the gain applies to the whole take, so each take keeps its own key-down/key-up balance. The build stops on a take whose key-up is more than 6 dB louder than its key-down (no gain can level it), and if any shipped stroke falls outside the band (with 0.5 dB of slack for measuring before the final gain). As shipped, the key-downs span 6.0 dB, with a median of -26.9 LK and a power average of -25.6 LK at volume 1.0; the key-ups have a median of -30.2 LK and none is above -23.2 LK.

## How each file was made

All files: decoded with ffmpeg at the download's own sample rate (44.1 kHz, or 48 kHz for the Enter and backspace previews; no resampling), channels averaged to mono, 30 Hz 2nd-order Butterworth high-pass (also removes DC), split into key-down and key-up as above, each stroke cut as listed (0.5 ms raised-cosine fade-in before the onset; raised-cosine fade-out ending on an exact zero; at most 0.4 s), one gain per take (the levelling gain above, times one gain shared by all StavSounds takes) or per source (Enter, backspace), then one headroom trim for the whole pack, written as 16-bit PCM WAV at the download's rate. No other processing.

Gains: the 10 levelled StavSounds takes share one gain that aims the key-downs' median peak at -6 dBFS, capped so that no StavSounds file (key-down or key-up) peaks above -0.5 dBFS. After levelling, the key-downs span about 10 dB of peak level and the key-ups about 12 dB. After the headroom trim below, the key-downs' median peak is -9.0 dBFS. The Enter's key-down peaks 1 dB above that median and the backspace key's level with that median; their key-ups keep their recorded level next to their key-down. Headroom: the mixer clips hard at 0 dBFS, resampling to the device rate can peak between samples, and the runtime adds up to +6% of random volume per keystroke. So every gain is then scaled by -1.01 dB, which keeps the loudest file's true peak (4x oversampled) at -1.51 dBFS, and at -1.00 dBFS at the top of the volume variation (the rule is at most -1 dBFS). No sample reaches full scale (the highest sample peak is -1.51 dBFS). The Gain column is the total.

`preview.wav` (SHA-256 `33ba08234f001e3129dee37684362fad8417b0da17ab6887be4c84bac6744363`): just under 2 s of typing at 44100 Hz rendered from the pack's own files (4 keys, space, 3 keys, space, 3 keys, Enter, each with its key-up; 60–120 ms holds, 80–200 ms between presses, ±6% volume per stroke, fixed random seed; the 48 kHz Enter files are resampled to 44.1 kHz by ffmpeg for this mix only), scaled down only if it would peak above -1 dBFS.

## Loudness

`volume` in `pack.json` is 0.98 (-0.2 dB): a playback gain the app applies to the whole pack, so no audio file changes. Typing loudness is matched across the bundled packs so that switching packs does not jump in volume; the target is TakTak's reference typing level, -25.8 LK. Measured with `cargo run -p synth-packs --release -- loudness packs/tactile` (`tools/synth-packs/src/loudness.rs`): the K-weighted (ITU-R BS.1770) energy of the first 100 ms of the sample each alphanumeric key plays on press by default, power-averaged over the keys, on the samples as the app loads them at 48 kHz. The pack reads -26.1 LK as built and -26.2 LK at this volume; the loudest true peak at the top of the volume variation becomes -1.18 dBFS. `build.py` writes the volume (`VOLUME`), so a rebuild keeps it.

## Not used

- StavSounds' "Keyboard_Tactile_13" (https://freesound.org/people/StavSounds/sounds/766629/, CC0; clatterbox's `down-02.mp3`, SHA-256 `ec4d29b88d66d478e269d15456a9bec695fd8efd03ecbe04ac3c9595733443b2`): a soft key-down that never bottomed out, then a hard top-out, so the keystroke's click would come late, when the key is let go. Measured as under "Levelling", its key-down is -9.3 dB from the median of the used takes and its key-up +16.5 dB from its key-down; no levelling gain fits it.
- StavSounds' "Keyboard_Tactile_9" (https://freesound.org/people/StavSounds/sounds/766640/, CC0; clatterbox's `down-12.mp3`, SHA-256 `813ef394935bd69d91693a7384361b9b8c2fbc4a56b9a205a22cdf63accb9c64`): the quietest key-down by far, with a key-up louder than it: it would need by far the largest levelling boost, and its click would still come late, on the key-up. Measured as under "Levelling", its key-down is -11.1 dB from the median of the used takes and its key-up +5.9 dB from its key-down; levelling it would take +8.1 dB.
- Foxfire-'s "Keyboard - Key release" (https://freesound.org/people/Foxfire-/sounds/570755/, CC0; clatterbox's `up-01.mp3`): a key-up from a different keyboard (Cherry MX Brown). Every take above carries its own key-up, so the pack uses those instead.
- Foxfire-'s matching press, "Keyboard - Press down" (https://freesound.org/people/Foxfire-/sounds/570754/, CC0): Freesound needs a login to download it, and on 2026-10-02 no mirror without a login was found.
